name: Calcium dobesilate

sources.citation: AEMPS. Doxium Fuerte 500 mg hard capsules: product information, revised June 2017. Accessed November 25, 2026. Spanish reference, not proof of identical Philippine instructions.
Haritoglou C, et al. Effect of calcium dobesilate on occurrence of diabetic macular oedema (CALDIRET study): randomized double-blind placebo-controlled multicenter trial. Lancet. 2009. PMID 19376452.
Strong Negative Interference by Calcium Dobesilate in Sarcosine Oxidase Assays for Serum Creatinine Involving the Trinder Reaction. Medicine. 2015. PMID 26061311.

draft_notes: Foreign reference labeling is explicitly attributed; current Philippine insert and individual clinical assessment remain necessary. No dialysis schedule is inferred.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive overview, safety and evidence with product-scope limitations.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

overview.mechanism: The Spanish reference describes effects on microcirculatory parameters; such effects do not by themselves establish prevention of vision-threatening outcomes [[DOXSP,CALDIRET]].
uses: Spanish reference indication: nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy. Verify the local insert; the cited large trial did not show prevention of clinically significant macular edema [[DOXSP,CALDIRET]].

contraindications: Spanish reference: hypersensitivity to calcium dobesilate or excipients [[DOXSP]].

serious: Agranulocytosis and severe hypersensitivity, including anaphylaxis, require prompt assessment [[DOXSP]].
common: Gastrointestinal symptoms and headache are listed in the Spanish reference [[DOXSP]].

monitoring: Fever or inflamed oral mucosa can signal agranulocytosis: stop treatment, seek urgent assessment and obtain a blood count as directed in the cited label [[DOXSP]].
Tell the laboratory about calcium dobesilate: susceptible enzymatic creatinine assays can read falsely low; clinical interpretation must account for the measurement method [[DOBLAB]].

renal: Spanish labeling advises caution in renal impairment; severe impairment requiring dialysis calls for adjustment according to creatinine clearance, but no numerical schedule is supplied [[DOXSP]].
A lower measured creatinine during exposure can reflect analytical interference rather than improved kidney function [[DOBLAB]].
pregnancy: Spanish labeling says not to administer during pregnancy [[DOXSP]].
breastfeeding: Spanish labeling calls for discontinuing treatment or breastfeeding [[DOXSP]].

rows.design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; 635 adults with type 2 diabetes and mild-to-moderate nonproliferative retinopathy; up to five years.
rows.findings: Clinically significant macular edema occurred in 86 treated and 69 placebo participants; hazard ratio 1.32 (95% CI 0.96–1.81). No risk reduction was demonstrated.
rows.limitations: These results concern the studied retinal endpoint, not every proposed vascular indication.

rows.design: Laboratory experiments plus healthy-participant and patient samples.
rows.intervention: Several sarcosine oxidase enzymatic assays compared with reference methods.
rows.findings: Negative interference varied substantially by assay; creatinine could be falsely low.
rows.limitations: No universal numerical correction applies to every platform or patient.
